description: 🚀 We are Tesseract.exe, a Brazilian team of developers and creative problem-solvers passionate about space, technology, and education. For NASA Space Apps, we're building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: an interactive experience that helps young explorers learn about life on the Moon or Mars through science and play. We welcome teammates skilled in game development, UI/UX, 2D/3D art, astronomy, and storytelling. Join our mission—gravity won't hold us back! 🌌
summary:
AstroLab – Learning Through Space Exploration

AstroLab is an interactive 3D educational game developed using Unity and Blender that transforms learning about space exploration into an immersive experience. Players take on the role of astronauts and experience different stages of a space mission: training on Earth, traveling through space, landing on the Moon, and surviving at a lunar base. Throughout the journey, they must solve challenges, repair equipment, manage resources, and prepare the base for the arrival of a new crew.

The project addresses the challenge of making science education more accessible, engaging, and practical, especially for children and young learners. Through gamification, players explore concepts related to astronomy, physics, technology, and sustainability while developing critical thinking, planning, and problem-solving skills.

AstroLab is important because it connects space science with interactive learning, inspiring curiosity and encouraging interest in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). More than just a game, AstroLab demonstrates that education can be an adventure, inspiring future generations to explore knowledge and imagine their role in the future of space exploration.
details:
AstroLab – Project Details

AstroLab is an immersive 3D educational game designed to make space exploration and scientific learning more accessible, interactive, and engaging, especially for children and young students. By combining storytelling, realistic space missions, and gamification, the project transforms complex scientific concepts into exciting, hands-on learning experiences.

How Does It Work?

Players take on the role of astronauts preparing for a mission to the Moon. Their journey begins on Earth, where they complete training activities inspired by real astronaut preparation programs. After training, players board a spacecraft, travel through space, experience a cinematic lunar landing, and begin their mission at a lunar research base.

Once on the Moon, players face challenges involving survival, resource management, equipment maintenance, and scientific exploration. They must monitor oxygen and energy supplies, repair solar panels, restore essential systems, and prepare the lunar base for the arrival of another crew.

Each challenge encourages players to apply scientific knowledge, logical reasoning, and problem-solving skills in an interactive environment.

Technology and Development

AstroLab is developed using Unity 6 and C# for gameplay mechanics, interactions, animations, and mission systems. Blender and Python are used for 3D modeling and procedural asset creation. The project also utilizes Unity's Universal Render Pipeline (URP), Cinemachine, custom shaders, and visual effects to create a stylized yet believable space environment.

Git and GitHub support collaborative development, allowing team members to work independently on different systems while maintaining a unified project.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes AstroLab unique is its combination of educational content with immersive gameplay. Rather than simply presenting scientific information, the game allows students to experience the challenges of space exploration through decision-making, experimentation, and interactive missions.

Its cartoon-realistic visual style balances scientific inspiration with an accessible and engaging design for younger audiences.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroLab aims to stimulate curiosity about astronomy, physics, engineering, technology, and space exploration while strengthening critical thinking, teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving abilities.

Our team prioritizes educational accessibility, scientific relevance, intuitive gameplay, visual consistency, and technical performance.

Ultimately, AstroLab seeks to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers by demonstrating that learning science can be as exciting as exploring another world.
